title: Local Hamiltonian ground-energy optimization

problem.name: Local Hamiltonian
problem.statement_latex: Given $H=\sum_{j=1}^m H_j$ on $n$ qubits, with constant-local terms of polynomially bounded norm, distinguish $\lambda_{\min}(H)\le a$ from $\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge b$, promised $b-a\ge1/\operatorname{poly}(n)$. Diagonal terms encode classical constraint optimization; noncommuting terms permit quantum witnesses. Complexity is measured in quantum gates or block-encoding queries and classical arithmetic operations at the required precision.
problem.statement_text: Given $H=\sum_{j=1}^m H_j$ on $n$ qubits, with constant-local terms of polynomially bounded norm, distinguish $\lambda_{\min}(H)\le a$ from $\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge b$, promised $b-a\ge1/\operatorname{poly}(n)$. Diagonal terms encode classical constraint optimization; noncommuting terms permit quantum witnesses. Complexity is measured in quantum gates or block-encoding queries and classical arithmetic operations at the required precision.

quantum.headline_latex: $O^*(2^{n/2})$ gates, energy filtering and amplitude amplification at inverse-polynomial precision.
quantum.details_latex: A purification of the maximally mixed state supplies ground-subspace overlap at least $2^{-n/2}$. In a guided-state regime, a preparable state with ground-state overlap amplitude $\gamma$, gap lower bound $\Delta$, and block encoding of $H/\alpha$ allows ground-state preparation in $\widetilde O(\alpha/(\gamma\Delta))$ block-encoding queries. The 2-local decision problem is QMA-complete, so a polynomial-time quantum solution would imply $\mathrm{QMA}=\mathrm{BQP}$.
quantum.headline_text: $O^*(2^{n/2})$ gates, energy filtering and amplitude amplification at inverse-polynomial precision.
quantum.details_text: A purification of the maximally mixed state supplies ground-subspace overlap at least $2^{-n/2}$. In a guided-state regime, a preparable state with ground-state overlap amplitude $\gamma$, gap lower bound $\Delta$, and block encoding of $H/\alpha$ allows ground-state preparation in $\widetilde O(\alpha/(\gamma\Delta))$ block-encoding queries. The 2-local decision problem is QMA-complete, so a polynomial-time quantum solution would imply $\mathrm{QMA}=\mathrm{BQP}$.

classical.details_latex: Each matrix-vector product costs $O(m2^n)$ operations; inverse-polynomial accuracy contributes polynomial overhead. State-vector memory is exponential. For the diagonal subfamily with $O(n)$ constant-arity terms and constant-bit integer weights, a linear-size threshold circuit and sparse counting instead give exact minimization in $\operatorname{poly}(n)2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ time.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant for the generic noncommuting comparison. Guided-state preparation is polynomial when its overlap, gap and block encoding have polynomial costs.

evidence.description_latex: Proved algorithmic upper bounds and QMA-completeness; the generic runtime advantage is a comparison with known classical algorithms.

hardware.description_latex: A fault-tolerant implementation uses $2n$ qubits for the mixed-state purification, plus filtering and arithmetic ancillas. The generic method has exponential depth; guided-state resources depend on $\gamma$, $\Delta$ and precision.
